data.long_meaning: Zophia or Zophah is a Hebrew name meaning 'God has heard'. It is a feminine form of the name Zophar, meaning 'little bird'. In the Bible, Zophar is one of Job's three friends who come to comfort him during his suffering. The name Zophia became popular in England in the late 19th century and has been used ever since. The name Zophina carries the meaning “God has heard” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Zophina usually hope their child will grow to embody god has heard and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Zophina evokes a sense of hope and faith in God, as it reminds us that He is always listening and attentive to our prayers.
data.etymology: Zophina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God has heard.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Zophina total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_english.name: Zophina
in_english.meaning: woman of prophecy, woman of timing, wise woman, virtuous woman, woman of hope
in_english.long_meaning: The name Zophina is derived from the Hebrew word 'tsufan', which means 'to wait or to expect', and is associated with women who were prophets or wise women. In the Christian tradition, Zophina is a name given to women who were devoted to God and had a strong faith. They were women who were virtuous, hopeful, and faithful, and who lived their lives according to their values and principles. The name Zophina is also associated with women who were known for their wisdom, their kindness, and their generosity. In modern times, the name Zophina is given to girls who are expected to grow up to be strong, independent women with a strong sense of purpose and direction.

historical_references.reference: The name Zophia or Zophina is mentioned in the Old Testament as the name of a daughter of King Solomon and the Shunammite woman. (1 Kings 1:12-13)
Zophia was also the name of a 5th century AD saint from Egypt. She was a virgin and a martyr, and her feast day is celebrated on April 19.
